metadata.author: Architecture Expert + UCE34 Framework
metadata.description: Systematic UCE34 analysis (Q1-Q34) for implementing Byzantine Royal × macOS premium design system in Leptos 0.7. Capsule-driven theming with glassmorphism, holographic gradients, and metallic effects.

question.text: What is the core problem or need?
question.answer:
Implement premium Byzantine Royal × macOS design system in Leptos 0.7 web framework requiring: - Consistent theming (colors, spacing, typography, animations) - Glassmorphism effects (multi-layer backdrop blur with 60fps performance) - Holographic gradients (multi-layer animated gradients, continuous updates) - Metallic text effects (deterministic shimmer timing, Q16.16 fixed-point) - Responsive layout state (breakpoint management, atomic coordination)
User need: Premium visual experience with macOS-quality polish at web-scale performance

question.text: What's the specific performance target or latency requirement?
question.answer:
- Theme lookup: <5ns (accessed on every render, must be instant) - Blur calculation: <50ns for 4 layers (60fps = 16ms budget, hundreds of elements) - Gradient update: O(1) incremental (continuous animations, no frame drops) - Layout query: <10ns (responsive breakpoint checks on resize) - Shimmer timing: <20ns deterministic (fixed-point Q16.16, no drift)
Reality: Web framework (Leptos) has WASM overhead (~10ns per call), so absolute targets must account for boundary crossing. Capsules minimize crossings via batched reads.

question.text: What are the constraints (hardware, memory, dependencies)?
question.answer:
Hardware: - Client-side WASM (single-threaded, no SIMD in stable WASM, ~2GB memory limit) - Desktop browsers (Chrome/Firefox/Safari, all modern) - Mobile browsers (iOS Safari, Android Chrome, limited GPU)
Memory: - Theme capsule: <1KB (design tokens, accessed globally) - Glassmorphism: ~256B per element (4 layers × 64B) - Holographic: ~128B per gradient (streaming state) - Layout state: 64B (breakpoints, flags) - Total budget: <100KB for design system (thousands of components)
Dependencies: - Leptos 0.7 (reactive framework, Signal-based) - No unsafe code (WASM sandbox restrictions) - No nightly features (stable Rust for WASM target) - Zero external CSS framework (capsule-driven only)

question.text: What would success look like?
question.answer:
Measurable success criteria: 1. Performance: 60fps animations (no frame drops, <16ms frame time) 2. Memory: <100KB design system overhead (scales to 1000+ components) 3. Consistency: 100% design token coverage (no magic numbers in components) 4. Maintainability: Single source of truth (ThemeCapsule, no scattered constants) 5. Type safety: Compile-time verification (verify_capsule_properties! catches misalignment)
User experience: - Instant theme switching (<100ms visual update) - Smooth animations (no stuttering, 60fps target) - Premium polish (blur/gradient/shimmer quality matches native macOS)

question.text: What would failure look like?
question.answer:
Performance failures: - Frame drops during animations (<60fps, visible stuttering) - Slow theme switching (>500ms, user-perceivable lag) - Memory bloat (>500KB, impacts page load time)
Architectural failures: - Scattered design tokens (magic numbers in 100+ components) - Inconsistent styling (color drift, spacing mismatches) - WASM boundary overhead (excessive Rust↔JS calls, >1ms per operation)
Developer experience failures: - Complex API (developers bypass design system, use inline CSS) - Brittle theming (color changes require editing 50+ files) - Type confusion (runtime errors from incorrect capsule usage)

question.text: What is the baseline or current solution?
question.answer:
Current baseline (typical web development): - CSS variables for theming (--color-primary, accessed via var()) - JavaScript-driven animations (requestAnimationFrame loops) - CSS backdrop-filter for glassmorphism (GPU accelerated, but no control) - Inline style attributes for dynamic values
Performance baseline: - CSS variable access: ~50ns (browser overhead) - backdrop-filter calculation: ~5-10ms (GPU, browser-controlled) - JS animation frame: ~16ms budget (60fps, includes all work) - Theme switching: ~100-500ms (CSS recalculation cascade)
Key weakness: No systematic approach. Design tokens scattered across CSS files. Each component reimplements blur/gradient logic. No type safety.

question.text: What are the key challenges or pain points?
question.answer:
Challenge 1: WASM boundary overhead - Rust capsules live in WASM, Leptos components in Rust, DOM in JavaScript - Every capsule→CSS conversion crosses boundary (~10-50ns overhead) - Solution: Batch reads (load all theme tokens in single call, not per-property)
Challenge 2: GPU vs CPU blur - CSS backdrop-filter uses GPU (fast, ~5ms) - Rust capsules CPU-only in WASM (no GPU access) - Solution: Capsules compute blur PARAMETERS (radius, opacity, layers), CSS applies actual blur via backdrop-filter
Challenge 3: Animation timing - Leptos reactive signals fire on every change - Holographic gradients need continuous updates (60fps) - Solution: T5 Streaming capsule with O(1) incremental updates, Signal only fires when visual change needed
Challenge 4: Deterministic shimmer - JavaScript timestamps drift (floating-point accumulation) - Metallic text needs deterministic timing (replay, testing) - Solution: T3 Fixed-Point Q16.16 for shimmer phase accumulation

question.text: What data access patterns exist?
question.answer:
Pattern 1: Theme token lookup (read-heavy, global) - Accessed: Every component render (~100-1000 times per frame) - Write frequency: Rare (theme switch, ~once per session) - Access pattern: Random (different components need different tokens) - Optimization: T1 Atomic with cache-aligned struct, single read loads all needed tokens
Pattern 2: Blur calculations (compute-heavy, per-element) - Accessed: Every glassmorphism element (~10-100 per page) - Write frequency: Rare (window resize, theme change) - Access pattern: Sequential (iterate 4 layers per element) - Optimization: T2 SIMD for 4-layer parallel computation (but WASM lacks SIMD, fallback to scalar)
Pattern 3: Gradient animations (streaming, continuous) - Accessed: Every animation frame (60fps) - Write frequency: 60Hz (continuous updates) - Access pattern: Incremental (compute next gradient step from previous) - Optimization: T5 Streaming with O(1) incremental updates
Pattern 4: Layout breakpoints (query-heavy, resize events) - Accessed: Every layout calculation (~100+ per resize) - Write frequency: Rare (window resize only) - Access pattern: Binary search (find active breakpoint) - Optimization: T1 Atomic with bit-packed flags, single load checks all breakpoints

question.text: What are the computational patterns?
question.answer:
Pattern 1: Lockfree reads (theme tokens, layout state) - Multiple components read theme simultaneously - No writes during render (theme immutable until switch) - Tier: T1 Atomic with Relaxed loads (no synchronization overhead)
Pattern 2: Deterministic calculations (shimmer timing, blur radii) - Fixed-point arithmetic for drift-free accumulation - Must replay identically (testing, debugging) - Tier: T3 Fixed-Point Q16.16 (2-10× faster than float, zero drift)
Pattern 3: Incremental updates (holographic gradients) - Compute only changed pixels, not full re-render - O(1) per frame regardless of gradient complexity - Tier: T5 Streaming with window-based incremental computation
Pattern 4: Batch processing (glassmorphism for multiple elements) - Process 4 blur layers in parallel (but WASM lacks SIMD) - Could use T2 SIMD on native, T1 Atomic for WASM fallback - Tier: T1 Atomic (WASM), future T2 SIMD (when WASM supports it)

question.text: Which computational capsule tier transforms this problem?
question.answer:
Multi-tier architecture (T1, T3, T5 composition):
T1 Atomic - Theme tokens & layout state: - ThemeCapsule: Global design tokens (64B cache-aligned) - LayoutStateCapsule: Responsive breakpoints (64B cache-aligned) - Speedup: 3-10× vs mutex-protected theme (instant reads) - Why: Lockfree concurrent reads, zero allocation, <5ns access
T3 Fixed-Point - Deterministic timing: - MetallicTextCapsule: Shimmer phase accumulation (Q16.16) - Speedup: 5-10× vs float + zero drift - Why: Deterministic replay, no floating-point accumulation errors
T5 Streaming - Continuous animations: - HolographicGradientCapsule: Incremental gradient updates - Speedup: O(1) incremental vs O(n) full recalculation - Why: 60fps animations without recalculating entire gradient
T1 Atomic (fallback) - Glassmorphism: - GlassmorphismCapsule: Blur parameters (NOT actual blur) - Note: CSS backdrop-filter does actual GPU blur - Why: WASM lacks GPU access, capsule computes parameters only
Rationale: WASM constraints eliminate T2 SIMD (no stable SIMD), T4 Batch (single-threaded), T6 Mixed (can't compound without SIMD). Use T1 foundation with T3 determinism and T5 streaming where beneficial.

question.text: How does Rust fundamentally transform this problem?
question.answer:
Rust transformation 1: Type-safe design tokens - Traditional: CSS variables (strings, runtime errors) - Rust: Enum-based tokens, compile-time verification - Impact: Color typos caught at build time, not runtime
Rust transformation 2: Zero-cost abstractions - Traditional: CSS cascade (expensive recalculation) - Rust: Compile-time theme resolution, inline constants - Impact: Theme tokens become compile-time constants where possible
Rust transformation 3: Ownership-based capsules - Traditional: Global mutable state (theme switching race conditions) - Rust: Atomic capsules with Acquire/Release ordering - Impact: Thread-safe theme switching (future multi-threaded WASM)
Rust transformation 4: Pattern matching for breakpoints - Traditional: if/else chains for responsive logic - Rust: Match expressions with exhaustiveness checking - Impact: All breakpoints handled, compiler enforces coverage
Rust transformation 5: Fixed-point determinism - Traditional: JavaScript float accumulation drift - Rust: Q16.16 fixed-point with integer arithmetic - Impact: Shimmer timing perfectly deterministic (replay, testing)

question.text: How can unstable/nightly features enhance this?
question.answer:
Note: WASM target restricts to stable Rust only. Nightly features listed for future native desktop app or when WASM stabilizes features.
Future enhancement 1: portable_simd (T2) - Feature: SIMD vectorization for blur calculations - Impact: 4 blur layers in parallel (4× speedup potential) - Status: Awaiting WASM SIMD stabilization
Future enhancement 2: const_fn_floating_point (T0/T3) - Feature: Compile-time gradient interpolation - Impact: Holographic gradient colors computed at build time - Status: Stable Rust 1.82+ has this (use immediately)
Future enhancement 3: const_trait_impl - Feature: Const trait implementations for capsules - Impact: verify_capsule_properties! enforced at const eval - Status: Unstable, not critical (runtime verification sufficient)
Current approach: Stable Rust only for WASM compatibility. All optimizations use stable features (atomics, const fn, fixed-point). Nightly features deferred until WASM target supports them.

question.text: What's the simplest approach that solves 80% of the problem?
question.answer:
Simplest MVP (minimal viable premium design):
1. ThemeCapsule only (defer blur/gradient/shimmer) - 64B cache-aligned struct with 10 core colors - Atomic reads (no theme switching initially) - Impact: 80% of design consistency from color tokens alone
2. CSS for visual effects (defer capsule-driven effects) - Use CSS backdrop-filter for glassmorphism (good enough) - Use CSS gradients for holographic (static, not animated) - Skip metallic text (nice-to-have, not critical) - Impact: Visual quality acceptable, just not animated
3. Signal-based breakpoints (defer LayoutStateCapsule) - Use Leptos built-in window resize Signal - Simple if/else for breakpoint logic - Impact: Responsive works, just not optimized
THEN iterate: - Phase 2: Add LayoutStateCapsule (optimize breakpoints) - Phase 3: Add HolographicGradientCapsule (animated gradients) - Phase 4: Add MetallicTextCapsule (shimmer effects) - Phase 5: Add GlassmorphismCapsule (if CSS insufficient)
This follows IMPL-2 V3.1: Build cutting-edge, but validate each tier independently. Don't over-engineer all 5 capsules if ThemeCapsule alone solves 80% of design consistency.

question.text: Can we simplify interfaces to reduce cognitive load?
question.answer:
Simplification 1: Unified theme() accessor - Bad: theme.colors.primary.500, theme.spacing.md, theme.radius.lg - Good: theme(Token::ColorPrimary500), theme(Token::SpacingMd) - Impact: Single function, enum-driven, autocomplete-friendly
Simplification 2: Derive-based capsule creation - Bad: Manual capsule construction with 10 fields - Good: #[derive(ThemeCapsule)] on config struct - Impact: Zero boilerplate, compiler generates capsule code
Simplification 3: CSS string generation - Bad: Manual string formatting for each CSS property - Good: impl Display for ThemeCapsule (automatic CSS generation) - Impact: theme.to_string() generates complete CSS custom properties
Simplification 4: Component integration - Bad: Explicit capsule.load() calls in every component - Good: use_theme() hook returns theme capsule (Leptos context) - Impact: Components access theme naturally via context API
IMPL-2 compliance: Hide capsule complexity behind clean APIs. Developers use theme(Token::Color), not raw atomic loads.

question.text: What are the practical constraints we must respect?
question.answer:
Constraint 1: WASM single-threaded (no parallelism) - Implication: No T4 Batch, no multi-threaded SIMD - Workaround: Use T5 Streaming for async-like incremental work
Constraint 2: No unsafe code in WASM sandbox - Implication: No raw pointer manipulation, no transmute - Workaround: Use safe atomics (std::sync::atomic), verified capsules
Constraint 3: Leptos reactive system (Signal-based) - Implication: Capsules must integrate with Signal<T> - Workaround: Capsule updates trigger Signal writes, Leptos handles reactivity
Constraint 4: CSS for actual rendering (WASM can't draw pixels) - Implication: Capsules compute PARAMETERS, CSS renders effects - Workaround: Capsules generate CSS custom properties, browser applies styles
Constraint 5: Memory limit (~2GB WASM) - Implication: Design system must be <100KB - Workaround: Cache-aligned capsules prevent bloat, fixed-size structs only

question.text: How do we automatically verify correctness?
question.answer:
Verification 1: Compile-time capsule properties - Tool: verify_capsule_properties!(ThemeCapsule, 64, 64) - Catches: Misalignment, incorrect size, padding errors - Impact: Capsule bugs caught at build time, not runtime
Verification 2: Property-based testing - Tool: proptest (1000+ random theme configurations) - Catches: Edge cases (zero opacity, invalid colors) - Impact: Theme switching robustness validated statistically
Verification 3: Visual regression testing - Tool: percy.io or similar (screenshot comparison) - Catches: Unintended visual changes - Impact: Theme updates don't break existing components
Verification 4: Performance benchmarks - Tool: B32 framework (Criterion, 95% CI) - Catches: Performance regressions - Impact: Capsule updates maintain <5ns theme access target
T28 compliance: Unit tests (capsule internals), property tests (theme logic), integration tests (Leptos components), production tests (visual regression).

question.text: How do we design for auditability and compliance?
question.answer:
Not applicable for design system (Q34 is for SOX/GDPR/HIPAA compliance).
Design systems don't require audit trails. However, theme versioning could use T0 Auditable patterns for design history:
Optional enhancement (future): - Theme change log (who, when, what changed) - A/B test tracking (which theme variant shown to user) - Accessibility compliance (WCAG color contrast validation)
Current scope: Skip Q34. Focus on Q10-Q12 (capsule architecture) and Q28-Q33 (simplicity, constraints, verification).

capsule.name: ThemeCapsule
capsule.description: Global design token storage with lockfree atomic reads. Single source of truth for colors, spacing, typography, borders, shadows, and animations. Cache-aligned for instant access (<5ns).
capsule.tier-justification: T1 Atomic: Lockfree concurrent reads from multiple components. Zero allocation. Atomic theme switching with Acquire/Release ordering. 3-10× faster than mutex-protected global.

capsule.name: LayoutStateCapsule
capsule.description: Responsive breakpoint state with bit-packed flags for instant queries. Atomic updates on window resize. Single atomic load checks all breakpoints (<10ns).
capsule.tier-justification: T1 Atomic: Lockfree reads during layout calculations. Bit-packed flags enable single atomic load for all breakpoint checks. No mutex overhead.

capsule.name: MetallicTextCapsule
capsule.description: Deterministic shimmer effect timing using Q16.16 fixed-point arithmetic. Zero drift for perfect replay and testing. Phase accumulation <20ns.
capsule.tier-justification: T3 Fixed-Point: Deterministic timing (same input → same output). No floating-point drift. 5-10× faster than float with zero accumulation errors. Critical for animation replay.

capsule.name: HolographicGradientCapsule
capsule.description: Incremental gradient animation with O(1) per-frame updates. Streaming computation avoids full gradient recalculation. 60fps continuous updates.
capsule.tier-justification: T5 Streaming: O(1) incremental updates per frame regardless of gradient complexity. Avoids O(n) full recalculation. Window-based streaming enables 60fps animations without performance degradation.

capsule.name: GlassmorphismCapsule
capsule.description: Blur parameter computation (NOT actual blur). Stores blur radius, opacity, and layer configuration. CSS backdrop-filter applies actual GPU blur.
capsule.tier-justification: T1 Atomic: Lockfree parameter storage. Note: WASM cannot do actual blur (no GPU access). This capsule computes blur PARAMETERS (radius, opacity, layers), then CSS applies backdrop-filter. Future: T2 SIMD for multi-layer parameter calculation when WASM supports SIMD.
capsule.note: This capsule does NOT perform actual blur (WASM lacks GPU access). It computes blur PARAMETERS which are then applied via CSS backdrop-filter. This is the correct architecture for WASM constraints.

question.text: What components are being connected?
question.answer: Component A: Design system capsules (ThemeCapsule, LayoutStateCapsule, etc) Component B: Leptos 0.7 components (NavBar, Hero, Button, etc) Dependency: B depends on A (one-way, components consume capsules) Owner: Same team

question.text: What problem does integration solve?
question.answer: Problem: Inconsistent styling across components (magic numbers, color drift) Gap: No systematic design token access Expected improvement: 100% design token coverage, <5ns theme access User need: Premium visual consistency with instant theme switching

question.text: Is integration actually necessary?
question.answer:
Alternatives considered: 1. CSS variables only → No type safety, 50ns access overhead (rejected) 2. Inline styles → Code duplication, no consistency (rejected) 3. Tailwind CSS → External dependency, not capsule-driven (rejected) 4. Capsule-driven theming → Type-safe, <5ns access, single source of truth (APPROVED)
Cost of not integrating: Inconsistent design, slow theme switching, no type safety

question.text: Are architectural patterns compatible?
question.answer:
Capsules: Lockfree atomic reads, cache-aligned, deterministic Leptos: Reactive Signal-based, WASM-compiled Rust
Compatibility: ✅ YES - Both Rust (zero FFI overhead) - Capsules provide data, Signals trigger reactivity - Lockfree reads compatible with Signal subscriptions
Integration pattern: Capsule updates → Signal::set() → Leptos re-renders

question.text: Are performance characteristics compatible?
question.answer:
Capsules: <5ns theme access, <50ns updates Leptos: ~100ns Signal read, ~1μs component render
Performance tier compatibility: - Capsule read (<5ns) + Signal overhead (~100ns) = ~105ns total - Budget: <16ms per frame (60fps) - Hundreds of components × 105ns = ~10μs << 16ms budget
Compatibility: ✅ YES (capsule overhead negligible in render budget)

question.text: Are error handling strategies compatible?
question.answer:
Capsules: Result<T, CapsuleError> for fallible operations Leptos: Result<T, E> for component logic
Compatibility: ✅ YES - Both use Result<T, E> - Error propagation via ? operator - Leptos ErrorBoundary catches panics if needed

question.text: Are concurrency models compatible?
question.answer:
Capsules: Send + Sync (lockfree atomics) Leptos: Single-threaded WASM (but future multi-threaded support)
Compatibility: ✅ YES - Capsules are Send + Sync (future-proof) - Current WASM single-threaded (no contention) - Future multi-threaded WASM will work correctly (lockfree design)

question.text: What race conditions or deadlocks could occur?
question.answer:
Capsule architecture: 100% lockfree (NO mutex/RwLock) - No locks → No deadlocks (impossible) - Atomic operations → No data races - Generation counters → No ABA problems - Acquire/Release ordering → Proper synchronization
Compatibility: ✅ SAFE (lockfree mandate prevents deadlocks/races)
This question is SKIPPED per I20-Capsule guidelines (lockfree = no deadlocks).

question.text: What tests validate the integration?
question.answer:
T28 4-tier testing:
Unit tests (Q1-Q7): - ThemeCapsule: Color packing/unpacking, atomic reads - LayoutStateCapsule: Breakpoint flag logic - MetallicTextCapsule: Q16.16 phase accumulation
Property tests (Q8-Q14): - 1000+ random theme configurations - Determinism verification (same inputs → same outputs)
Integration tests (Q15-Q21): - Leptos components with ThemeCapsule context - Theme switching triggers Signal updates - CSS generation from capsule data
Production tests (Q22-Q28): - Visual regression (percy.io screenshots) - Performance benchmarks (B32, <5ns theme access) - Memory profiling (<100KB design system footprint)

question.text: What's the deployment strategy?
question.answer:
I20-Capsule decision rule:
IF compiles with verify_capsule_properties! ✓ AND property tests pass (1000+ cases) ✓ AND benchmarks validate performance (B32) ✓ THEN: Deploy at 100% immediately
Rationale: - Capsules are deterministic (tests predict production) - Compile-time verified (alignment bugs caught early) - No statistical uncertainty (not ML, not distributed system)
Deployment plan: 1. Run full test suite (T28 4 tiers) 2. Benchmark performance (B32 framework) 3. Deploy to production at 100% (no canary, no gradual rollout) 4. Rollback = git revert (unlikely needed, tests validate production)
No feature flags needed (deterministic = tests sufficient).

question.text: What's the rollback plan?
question.answer:
Rollback strategy: Git revert (deterministic capsules rarely fail in production)
Rollback triggers: - Performance regression (>5ns theme access, caught by monitoring) - Visual regression (screenshot diff, caught by visual tests) - Memory leak (>100KB design system, caught by profiling)
Rollback procedure: 1. git revert <commit-hash> 2. Deploy previous version (instant) 3. Investigate failure (local reproduction)
Note: Capsule determinism means production failures are rare (tests catch bugs). If tests pass, production will work (unlike ML/distributed systems).

Recommendation: APPROVED for immediate integration. Capsule architecture is compatible with Leptos framework. Follow I20-Capsule simplified deployment (no feature flags, deploy at 100% if tests pass).

conclusion.summary:
Premium design system architecture validated through UCE34 systematic analysis. Multi-tier capsule approach (T1 Atomic, T3 Fixed-Point, T5 Streaming) provides:
- Type-safe theming (<5ns access, 10× faster than CSS variables) - Deterministic animations (Q16.16 fixed-point, zero drift) - Incremental gradients (O(1) per-frame, 60fps sustained) - Lockfree coordination (100% lockfree, future multi-threaded WASM ready) - Compile-time verification (verify_capsule_properties! catches bugs early)
I20 integration analysis confirms compatibility with Leptos 0.7. Deploy at 100% if tests pass (deterministic capsules don't need gradual rollout).
conclusion.tier-selections: - T1 Atomic: ThemeCapsule (global tokens), LayoutStateCapsule (breakpoints), GlassmorphismCapsule (blur parameters) - T3 Fixed-Point: MetallicTextCapsule (deterministic shimmer timing) - T5 Streaming: HolographicGradientCapsule (incremental gradient updates)
conclusion.next-steps: 1. Implement Phase 1 MVP (ThemeCapsule, 1 week) 2. Validate performance targets (B32 benchmarks, <5ns theme access) 3. Deploy to production (I20-Capsule: 100% rollout if tests pass) 4. Iterate through Phases 2-5 (responsive, gradients, shimmer, blur)
